market_summary: US September PPI ran far hotter than expected: +1.3% m/m (0.5-0.6% expected), the biggest jump since March 2022, and 6.3% y/y, with core +0.7% (0.3% expected); retail sales rose 0.8% (0.3-0.4% expected) but the control group only 0.1% (0.3% expected), jobless claims were 199K, Philly Fed 20.9 (32 expected) and Empire State 25.5 (10.3 expected). Bonds rallied anyway, the 10-year falling about 10bp to 5.09%, and money rotated out of chips into old-economy names: Thursday's close was S&P 500 +0.33% to 7,744.06, Nasdaq +0.08% to 26,713.03 and Dow +1.08% to 52,177.69, while the chip index fell 0.88% for a seventh straight loss, TSMC's ADR fell 1.8% despite its record quarter, Nvidia -1.8%, Dell -6.8%, HPE -7.1%, and CoreWeave closed +5.9% after Jensen Huang backed it. CME FedWatch put an Oct 28 hike at about 30-34% after the data and at least one hike by December near 94%; Hammack said the Fed may need to move more if inflation expectations slip, and Warsh in Bangkok declined to signal October, saying the Fed will 'make judgements at the October and December meeting'. Friday in Asia chips steadied rather than rebounded: KOSPI +2.05% as foreigners turned net buyers after eight selling sessions (Samsung +2.6%, SK hynix +0.8% after -10-11% Thursday), Taiex +0.3% to 47,111.26 (TSMC -0.8%), Nikkei up about 1.4-1.9%, Shanghai about +1% to 3,742.66, Hang Seng +1.2% to 24,353.69 (afternoon) and ASX 200 +1.1% to 8,812.9, while Jakarta fell more than 10% on an MSCI downgrade warning. US futures were little changed; Brent was about $105.5 and WTI $97.4 (both about -0.5%) after WTI rose 2.8% Thursday on an 8.5M-barrel US crude draw and Trump floated easing shadow-fleet tanker sanctions; spot gold about $4,180 (+0.2%), bitcoin about $82,000. Next: import prices 23:30 AEDT tonight and industrial production 00:15 AEDT Sat; US open 00:30 AEDT Sat; options expiry Fri US (close 07:00 AEDT Sat); FOMC blackout from Sat Oct 17; China Q3 GDP, retail sales and industrial output 13:00 AEDT Mon Oct 19; Netflix 07:01 AEDT Wed Oct 21; SAP 07:05, Meta and TI 07:30, IBM and Lam 08:00, Tesla 08:30 AEDT Thu Oct 22; AU CPI 11:30 AEDT Wed Oct 28; Fed decision 05:00 AEDT Thu Oct 29; Alphabet 07:30, ServiceNow 08:00 and Microsoft 08:30 AEDT Thu Oct 29; US Q3 GDP and September PCE 23:30 AEDT Thu Oct 29; BoJ decision Fri Oct 30.

AMZN.reason: Up 0.3% Thursday as the Dow led (+1.1%) and the Nasdaq edged up 0.1% after hot PPI. No follow-up found on the WSJ-reported Decart talks (about $7 billion, unsigned). Q3 about Fri Oct 30 07:00 AEDT. Hold.

AXOS.reason: Up 1.1% Thursday as bonds rallied despite hot PPI (+1.3% m/m): the 10-year fell about 10 basis points to 5.09% and October hike odds eased to about 27%. Bank results were mixed (BNY +3.2%, Schwab -2.7%). Fiscal Q1 Fri Oct 30 08:00 AEDT. Hold.

BABA.reason: US ADR flat (-0.04%) Thursday. Tim Cook said in Shanghai that Apple Intelligence with Alibaba's Qwen is approved in China, with a beta due later in October, and Alibaba rose more than 2% at Friday's Hong Kong open. China Q3 GDP Mon Oct 19 13:00 AEDT. Hold.

ENPH.reason: Up 5.0% Thursday, recovering about half of Wednesday's 8.4% loss, as the 10-year yield fell about 10 basis points to 5.09%. No company news found. Q3 call Wed Oct 28 07:30 AEDT. Watch.

FIGR.reason: Up 10.5% Thursday, more than reversing Wednesday's 8.1% drop, as bond yields fell and Mortgage News Daily's 30-year dropped 0.12 points to 7.33%. No company news found. Still near its 52-week low, so the watch flag stays live; Q3 date not yet announced. Hold.

GOOGL.reason: Up 0.5% Thursday. TSMC raised its 2026 growth outlook to about 44% and said AI demand still exceeds supply, with AI accelerator growth likely above its mid-to-high-50s% long-run rate, which supports the TPU and Cloud build-out. Q3 results 07:30 AEDT Thu Oct 29. Add stays.

LDI.reason: Up 14.4% Thursday after falling 10.7% Wednesday, as Mortgage News Daily's 30-year fell 0.12 points to 7.33%, now more than 0.25 points below last week's highs. One day does not fix the problem: the stock remains under the NYSE minimum-price standard and MND warns the rate relief may not last. Trim.

META.reason: Down 0.1% Thursday. Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open-weight model built with Apple to run locally on Mac Studio, three days after the closed Muse Wonder. No New Mexico penalty ruling found. Q3 call Thu Oct 22 07:30 AEDT. Hold.

MRVL.reason: Down 1.7% Thursday as chip stocks lagged a broader rebound, after Wednesday's 8.7% fall. TSMC's call supports custom-chip demand: 2026 growth raised to about 44%, AI demand above supply, and CoWoS capacity to be expanded to meet orders. Hold.

MU.reason: Up 1.9% Thursday after an intraday fall of more than 6% to its lowest since Aug 11, ending a four-day losing run. HSBC and Daiwa said the CXMT threat is overstated for the next 2-3 years, but SK hynix still fell 1% and the stock is down about 10% since Oct 9. Taiwan union rally Mon Oct 19. Watch.

NFLX.reason: Up 2.9% Thursday, a second straight gain on down-to-flat tech days, with no new company news after Wednesday's confirmed 6% job cuts. Q3 results Wed Oct 21 07:00 AEDT. Hold into the print.

NVDA.reason: Fell 1.8% Thursday as chips lagged. Jensen Huang said CoreWeave needs no backstop and its cost of capital is falling, even as CoreWeave's credit swaps hit a record. TSMC said AI accelerator growth will probably beat its mid-to-high-50s% rate. GTC Berlin Oct 20-22. Hold.

RKT.reason: Up 5.1% Thursday, ending a five-day losing run, as Mortgage News Daily's 30-year fell 0.12 points to 7.33% and the 10-year yield dropped about 10 basis points. MND warns the rate relief is fragile because it rests on AI-selloff fears, not softer inflation. Q3 around Oct 29. Watch.

TSM.reason: TSMC raised 2026 growth to about 44% in US dollars, kept capex at $60-64 billion, and said AI demand still exceeds supply. The ADR still fell 1.8% Thursday and Taipei shares 0.8% Friday on a cautious 2027 tone and overseas-fab margin dilution of 3-4 points later in the decade. Add stays.

STRIPE.reason: No new round, tender or secondary mark found; the last company tender was February at $159 billion, so the mark multiple stays 2.27. No company news found for Oct 15-16. Hold.

OPENAI.reason: No close reported for the roughly $30 billion round at about $1.4 trillion pre-money, so the mark multiple stays 5.43. Nvidia is reportedly discussing backstopping $250 billion of OpenAI data-centre financing; neither side has confirmed. Hold.

headlines: Hot US PPI (+1.3% m/m) but bonds rallied, 10-year down 10bp to 5.09%; loanDepot +14%, Figure +10%, Rocket +5%.
TSMC lifted 2026 growth to about 44% and sees no AI slowdown, yet its ADR fell 1.8% and Taipei 0.8%.
Chip index fell a seventh straight day: Nvidia -1.8%, Marvell -1.7%; Micron closed +1.9% after a 6% intraday drop.
CoreWeave credit swaps hit a record before Huang backed it; shares closed +5.9%, the neocloud bellwether stays bearish.
Asia steadied Friday: KOSPI +2.05%, Samsung +2.6%, SK hynix +0.8% after Thursday's 10-11% falls.
Next: China Q3 GDP Mon 13:00 AEDT; Netflix Wed 07:00 AEDT; Meta Thu 07:30 AEDT; Fed decision Thu Oct 29 05:00 AEDT.
